To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the differential decondensation (uneven distribution of deoxyribo nucleoprotein fibrils along chromatid) is the main cause of G-bands formation in the chromosome.
the differential staining of mitotic chromosomes is caused by the differential decondensation, or unfolding, of the chromosomes.
differential decondensation is a cause of G-bands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ultrastructural basis of the G-banding of chromosomes.
a possible mechanism of G-banding.
the ultrastructural mechanisms of the formation of G-bands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
G-banding is caused by the differential decondensation and differential resistance to decondensation of DNP fibrils along chromosomes.
differential decondensation is the primary cause of G-bands.
differential staining of chromosomes is a consequence of differential decondensation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypotonic action on the living cell causes the decondensation of the chromatin, and the differential decondensation leads to the formation of the G-bands.
differential decondensation during hypotonic treatments may be a possible cause of differential staining.
the differential decondensation and differential staining are closely interrelated phenomena.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the hypotonic solution used to prepare cells for chromosome spreading is not just a passive agent that allows the chromosomes to be spread out, but rather it is an active agent that causes differential decondensation.
the G-bands are not a result of differential condensation of chromosomes but are a consequence of their differential decondensation.
the differential decondensation and restructuring of mitotic chromosomes in living cells may serve as the basis for differential staining of chromosomes.
